title: Differential Ingest Router & Adaptive Schema Validator
creator: Samir Patel
description:
Problem: Our usage event ingestion path receives highly heterogeneous payloads from multiple SDK versions, partner integrations, and the hosted API. Current strict schema gates cause high reject rates for benign changes (e.g., extra optional fields), while overly permissive validation increases downstream storage and analytics errors. We need an ingestion-side router and validator that applies adaptive strictness, performs lightweight pre-ingest checks, and surfaces schema drift for review without disrupting most customers.

Goal: Implement a 'Differential Ingest Router' that applies policy-driven validation tiers per route/customer and a complementary 'Adaptive Schema Validator' that can accept safe deviations, sample and quarantine unknown shapes, and emit drift signals to monitoring and the schema registry. The feature should be rollout-capable (feature flag + canary), add minimal latency, and provide clear observability and a migration path for customers currently failing strict validation.
rationale:
- Reduce false-positive rejects and developer support churn.
- Preserve downstream analytics integrity by quarantining and sampling unknown variants rather than dropping or blindly accepting them.
- Provide actionable drift detection so product/SDK teams can prioritize schema updates.
- Allow safe, incremental tightening of validation via canarying policies per customer/route.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end median added latency at router < 3ms for 95th percentile event size (payload <= 2KB)
Reject rate for previously-whitelisted customers remains < 0.2% after rollout in default mode
Sampling path captures >= 1% of events flagged as 'unknown shape' and stores them to quarantine bucket for 30 days
Drift dashboard surfaces top-5 drifting fields per route and triggers alerts when novel-field growth > 0.5% day-over-day
Feature flagging and canary controls available in Console for per-route policy toggles
Automated integration tests that replay historical event corpus show no data-loss regressions vs. baseline
tasks: Draft design doc and sequence diagram (Confluence) - owner: Diego
Schema registry API extension to return per-version field fingerprints - owner: Research
Implement lightweight pre-ingest validator in ingest-proxy (Go) with policy hooks
Build sampling/quarantine sink and TTL lifecycle for sampled events
Add drift detection job to telemetry pipeline (daily aggregate + trend alerts)
Create Console feature flag toggles and rollout UI for policies
End-to-end perf testing and load-run on dedicated staging cluster
Documentation and runbook for oncall and SRE handover
updates: 2026-01-20: Triage complete. Agreed to proceed with a two-path approach: fast pre-ingest validator + async sampler for unknowns.

2026-01-28: Spike finished. Prototype of pre-ingest validator implemented in ingest-proxy; median overhead measured ~1.8ms on local sim. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-proxy/pull/624
2026-02-03: Architecture review notes: prefer per-route policy store keyed by route-id and customer-id. Action: add policy cache with TTL to avoid registry hop on every event.
2026-02-09: Perf run on staging (10k rps) shows tail latency increase within SLO; discovered memory leak in sample buffer under burst - fix in progress (PR linked).
2026-02-15: Interim decision: default policy = 'lenient-with-sampling' for existing customers; strict mode only for new partners or opt-in via Console.
2026-02-22: Integration tests added for historical event corpus. Sampling sink written to quarantine GCS bucket 'quarantine/ingest/2026'. Preparing canary rollout plan for 5% traffic by 2026-03-01.
comments: PM (Arielle Chen): Important to surface SDK version in drift events so we can correlate with client releases.
Design (Farah Nguyen): Consider a compact fingerprint for fields (hash of name+type) to keep registry lookups small.
SRE (Liam O'Connor): Need alert thresholds and a throttling backpressure signal if quarantine writer falls behind.
Security (Jin Park): Confirm quarantine storage encryption and access controls; add KMS key usage in docs.
Reviewer (Nina Rossi): Minor comment on API contract for policy store; prefer explicit denylist over implicit null behavior.
observability: Alert: DriftNovelFieldRate > 0.5% day-over-day for 3 consecutive days
migration_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): Enable lenient-with-sampling for 5% traffic on non-critical routes; monitor for false positives
Phase 2 (Gradual Rollout): Increase to 25% then 75% over two weeks, surface per-customer dashboards for quarantined samples
Phase 3 (Policy Tuning): Work with SDK teams on resolving top drift causes and tighten policy on fixed routes
Rollback: Feature-flag can be set to bypass new validator entirely; fallback route to legacy pipeline retained for 48 hours
runbook: If quarantine writer falls behind or latency SLOs breach: 1) Flip per-cluster feature flag to bypass validator; 2) Increase canary sampling throttles to reduce load; 3) Notify SRE and PM with incident template including last 1k sampled events link.
notes: Avoid long-term storage of raw sampled events beyond 30 days unless requested by a customer investigation. Coordinate with legal for any retention exceptions.
